scope: Repository-owned document paths and repository-held reference copies in Markdown, text, HTML and PDF; inventory is exhaustive for these formats under the stated discovery/exclusion rules, not a sentence-by-sentence audit or proof of cryptographic correctness.

discovery.basis: union of tracked files and unignored untracked files, including hidden paths
discovery.ignoredUntrackedFiles: excluded; dependencies/build outputs and private local configuration are not repository documentation
discovery.trackedReferenceCopies: included but classified separately; inclusion does not imply Passport authorship

method.pdfSearch: pdftotext extraction followed by the same line-based searches; PDF line numbers refer to extracted text, not page numbers
method.htmlSearch: raw source search, including presentation text and embedded scripts
method.manualReview: Relevant sections and claims in identified specifications, current implementation documentation, dated experiment records and highlighted historical/design documents; not every matching sentence was independently validated. reviewDepth records this distinction.
method.noMatchesMeaning: No hit for the explicit patterns; not proof that a document contains no relevant natural-language claim.
method.platformProperties: Refer to research/ecc-validation.md; this document inventory does not rederive curve or proof-system guarantees.
actionsNotPerformed: No wallet secrets or existing browser profiles used

specificationAuthority: docs/mps-mip/README.md distinguishes canonical upstream mirrors from local working drafts and dated status records; this inventory does not independently certify present upstream acceptance.

findings.assessment: Already reflected in report; additional historical sources repeat older checks. Preserve dated observations rather than treating them as Compact 0.35 guarantees.

Distinguish supplied coordinates, normal decoder rejection, assigned subgroup representatives and coordinate/commitment binding. Current mixed-torsion witness normalisation is not an authorisation bypass.

Historical documents call persistentHash Poseidon; current Passport Schnorr challenges use SHA-256/grinding. Refer to the platform review for persistent versus transient hashing rather than deriving new cryptographic claims here.

Private keys are not required as witnesses, but the public site absolute claim that a prover never learns the key needs nonce-generation qualifications; zero/reused nonce signatures can disclose it as reproduced in the current report.

Knowledge-base statements that FROST reconstructs the full key during signing are incorrect. Standard FROST signs using shares; these claims also contradict other local documents. This is a documentation finding, not a demonstrated defect in the current reference signer.

Foundations plaintext recovery shares are explicitly documented as an insecure placeholder. Other prototypes and historical FROST research are distinct from the current reference account signature gates.
